paragraphs.title: Foundations of rates and linearizaton
paragraphs.p: Before analyzing complex equations, we must verify foundational rate notation and derivative operations. As a baseline mathematical exercise, let us consider the exponential function:

statement.p: Evaluate the instantaneous rate of change of the foundational exponential function: x(t) = e^{3t}

solution.p: To isolate the instantaneous rate component with respect to our independent time variable t, we apply the calculus chain rule operation to our candidate expression: \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(e^{3t}\right) = 3e^{3t}
We then substitute the original state definition expression directly back into the derivative result: \frac{dx}{dt} = 3x

The final derivative expression demonstrates an essential relationship: the rate of change of the system is directly proportional to the active state value itself. The stated rate balance law forms the literal core of first-order ordinary differential equations.
